action: Introduce appropriate cover crops or diversified vegetation.
reason: Additional plant biomass can increase organic inputs to soil and support soil structure and water retention.

action: Replace continuous monoculture with an appropriate diversified cropping system.
reason: Increasing vegetation diversity can provide additional habitat and biological resources while diversifying organic inputs to the soil.

action: Prioritize drought-adapted vegetation and practices that improve soil water retention.
reason: Limited water availability constrains plant establishment and can reduce habitat resources available to organisms.

action: Evaluate locally appropriate agroforestry where water availability and land use permit.
reason: Integrating woody vegetation can increase structural habitat diversity and provide additional organic inputs and microclimate variation.

action: Increase habitat heterogeneity using locally suitable vegetation patches, field margins, or diversified cropping.
reason: Greater habitat heterogeneity can provide a wider range of resources and niches for organisms.

action: Protect remaining habitat and restore ecological connections where feasible.
reason: Loss and fragmentation of habitat can reduce available resources and connectivity for species.

action: Identify and reduce unnecessary pollution pressure while monitoring soil and water conditions.
reason: Pollutants can affect organisms directly and alter soil or water conditions that support ecological communities.
